context.title: Babylon Is Taken
context.summary: The great oracle against Babylon begins: a nation from the north will capture the city, its gods Bel and Merodach will be shamed, and Israel and Judah will return together, weeping and seeking the Lord in an everlasting covenant. Babylon, 'the hammer of the whole earth,' will be broken for its pride.
context.background: Merodach (v. 2) is Marduk, Babylon's chief god, also called Bel ('lord'). Babylon fell to Cyrus of Persia in 539 BC with little fighting; its ruin and abandonment came gradually over later centuries. 'Merathaim' and 'Pekod' (v. 21) play on real regions of Babylonia, sounding like 'double rebellion' and 'punishment' in Hebrew.

customs.term: As the he goats before the flocks
customs.note: Male goats lead a flock out of the fold. The exiles should be first to leave Babylon.

watchFor: Israel as lost and scattered sheep (vv. 6, 17).
'How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder' (v. 23).
'As she hath done, do unto her' (vv. 15, 29), echoed in Revelation 18:6.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.summary: One of the “greater prophets” of the Old Testament, son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth (Jer. 1:1; 32:6). He was called to the prophetical office when still young (1:6), in the thirteenth year of Josiah (B.C. 628).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.summary: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.”

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: The Greek form of BABEL; Semitic form Babilu, meaning “The Gate of God.” In the Assyrian tablets it means “The city of the dispersion of the tribes.”

places.name: Zion
places.summary: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built. It was surrounded on all sides, except the north, by deep valleys, that of the Tyropoeon separating it from Moriah, which it surpasses in height by 105 feet.

places.name: Chaldea
places.summary: The southern portion of Babylonia, Lower Mesopotamia, lying chiefly on the right bank of the Euphrates, but commonly used of the whole of the Mesopotamian plain.

places.name: Assyria
places.summary: The name derived from the city Asshur on the Tigris, the original capital of the country, was originally a colony from Babylonia, and was ruled by viceroys from that kingdom.

places.name: Bashan
places.summary: Light soil, first mentioned in Gen. 14:5, where it is said that Chedorlaomer and his confederates “smote the Rephaim in Ashteroth,” where Og the king of Bashan had his residence.

places.name: Carmel
places.summary: A town in the hill country of Judah (Josh. 15:55), the residence of Nabal (1 Sam. 25:2, 5, 7, 40), and the native place of Abigail, who became David’s wife (1 Sam. 27:3).

places.name: Gilead
places.summary: Hill of testimony, (Gen. 31:21), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called “the mount of Gilead” (Gen. 31:25).

places.name: Merathaim
places.summary: Double rebellion, probably a symbolical name given to Babylon (Jer. 50:21), denoting rebellion exceeding that of other nations.

places.name: Pekod
places.summary: Probably a place in Babylonia (Jer. 50:21; Ezek. 23:23).

places.name: Gomorrah
places.summary: Submersion, one of the five cities of the plain of Siddim which were destroyed by fire (Gen. 10:19; 13:10; 19:24, 28). These cities probably stood close together, and were near the northern extremity of what is now the Dead Sea.

places.name: Sodom
places.summary: Burning; the walled, a city in the vale of Siddim (Gen. 13:10; 14:1-16). The wickedness of its inhabitants brought down upon it fire from heaven, by which it was destroyed (18:16-33; 19:1-29; Deut. 23:17).

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

events.title: Prophecies of Jeremiah
events.summary: Passage: Jeremiah 1:1–52:34. People: Jeremiah. Lasted about 67 years.
